column5: Anti-lysozyme VHH, PDB 1MEL chain A. Carries a second CDR1-CDR3 disulfide on top of the canonical one, and a 26-residue CDR3 - the clearest example of both in the app. The PDB entry continues GRYPYDVPDYGSGRA (HA tag) after VTVSS; that tail is not included here. DNA back-translated by this app, not the published gene.

Anti-GFP nanobody 'Enhancer', PDB 3K1K chain C. Scores 3/4 hallmarks, not 4/4 - a reminder that a genuine VHH need not be perfect on the tetrad. Short 8-residue CDR3. The PDB entry has a leading M and a trailing HHHHHH; neither is included here. DNA back-translated by this app, not the published gene.

Heavy variable domain of trastuzumab, PDB 1N8Z chain B, trimmed at the end of VTVSS. A conventional VH: 0/4 hallmarks and ~100% identity to a human germline. Use it to see what the app says about something that is not a VHH.
Light (kappa) variable domain of trastuzumab, PDB 1N8Z chain A, trimmed at the end of KVEIK. Classified as a light-chain V domain, so the antibody tabs skip it.

The whole heavy chain of PDB 1N8Z chain B: VH followed by CH1, 220 residues. The V domain covers 55% of it, so the app reports 'contains a V domain' and skips the VHH analyses - a multi-domain protein, not a single domain.

Hen egg-white lysozyme, PDB 1MEL chain C - the antigen cAbLys3 binds. Not an antibody domain at all, so only the generic analyses run. Its eight cysteines form four ordinary disulfides and are correctly not flagged as free thiols.
